Subject: Competitive eval follow-up: Atlas Retail — model quality & hallucination checks

Thanks again for the time today, Oliver and Susan — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

- Recap of ask: you want an apples-to-apples comparison of model quality vs the hyperscaler API you tested, focused on hallucination rate, factuality on product catalog Q&A, and regression checks against your existing prompt set. You also care about latency percentiles at your peak traffic profile.

- What we'll deliver: a short eval run (500 sample prompts + 100 long-context stress prompts) comparing Redwood-hosted run of the open model you prefer versus the hyperscaler endpoint you shared. We'll provide: hallucination/error rate, exact-match/ROUGE-L on the QA set, regeneration variance, and basic latency p50/p95 under a simulated load.

- Immediate asks for Atlas: please confirm the model variant you want us to run on (open model + quantization level), and attach the final prompt set if there were any edits after today. If you prefer, we can use the prompt set you dropped in Drive (we grabbed the link).

- Timeline: draft report by end of week (Fri EOD PST). If that works, we'll schedule a 30-min sync next Tue to walk results and discuss rollout/POC steps.

Attachments: initial eval script + example metrics (atlas_eval_results.csv stub) + redwood_vs_hyperscaler_comparison.pdf (summary template).

I'll hand technical coordination to Rishi (cc'd) to scope the exact test parameters.

Thanks —
Marissa

1) Sample size: the 500 sample prompts — is that 500 unique user queries sampled from our prod logs or 500 prompt/ground-truth pairs (we have ~12k labeled QA pairs)?
2) Hyperscaler endpoint: please use the version we mentioned on the call (MegaCloud v2.3, with default temperature 0.0).

We can provide a 500-with-held-from-prod subset if that helps (we prefer not to share full prod logs). If you need labels from us for the 100 long-context prompts, Susan can pull those.

Also, can you include hallucination examples inline in the report (so our PMs can see exact failing outputs)?

Hi Oliver / Susan — adding a bit more technical detail and the concrete test plan so you know what we'll run.

Planned tests (high level):
- Quality/regression: run your 500 withheld labeled QA pairs; compute exact-match + F1 (token overlap) + ROUGE-L. Highlight any regression where Redwood output score < hyperscaler by > 5 points.
- Hallucination checks: we will run the 500 QA prompts plus an additional 100 hard prompts where the correct answer is "no info" or expects a grounded fact. We'll mark hallucination when the model asserts unsupported facts or invents product features. We'll include the top 10 hallucination examples in the report with context.
- Prompt sensitivity: run 3 paraphrases per prompt to estimate variance/hallucination sensitivity.
- Latency: p50/p95 at 1x and 5x your stated traffic (we'll simulate with Redwood's load harness).
- Throughput/cost: basic per-token cost estimate using your traffic profile.

Data & access: we can work off the Drive link Marissa shared. If you prefer secure transfer, we can accept a password-protected S3 bucket or a signed DocuSign transfer link.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Dry-run + sanity check (small batch of 50 prompts) within 24 hours after we get the samples.
- Full run and draft PDF report by Fri EOD PST.

Oliver — for sample-format confirmation: if you can drop the 500 withheld pairs as a CSV (id, prompt, ground_truth) in the Drive folder, we'll kick off the dry-run as soon as it's there.

I'll own the run and the metric extraction. Reaching out to Aditya for tooling support on the latency harness.

Best,
Rishi
